claims: n-269-candidate.yaml is a packing.squares:Witness/v2 file (corners, rational scalars, 269 squares) whose exact rational side, rounded up at 12 places, #967 prints as the bound, 16.889730073596; the issue and README also print the exact side as 16.889730073595636. Its exact coordinates were produced by this repository's packing-witness promote --strategy robust-rational at 0352d755 from the lab's decimal pose, n-269-decimal-pose.yaml, with center_dilation '1' and no dilation: pairs separated by at least about 2e-13, the squares that set the left wall, the bottom wall and the side touching them exactly, and other squares near a wall clearing it by up to about 1e-12. An upper bound only: no KKT, local-optimality, rigidity or global-optimality claim.

n269-witness.json is the same file as JSON. packing-witness-verify.txt is the author's run of this repository's packing-witness verify at 0352d755 on the witness placed under packing/witnesses/known-best/ (VERIFIED, exact-algebraic, 36046 pairs); sqcheck-output.txt is the author's run of verifier/sqcheck.py, an exact checker the source says was written separately from this repository's code (VALID, exact rational, the exact side rounded up at 15 places). The issue says sqcheck.py also certified the decimal pose in interval arithmetic at its own side before promotion. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.

The issue and README say the packing was found by an AI-run column-band designer, new for this filing, with no donor packing: tilted squares stand in columns across a band along the diagonal at unit pitch, each column a stack of 1 to 3 squares sliding on its own; the axis-parallel squares sit on the two wall-anchored staircase lattices; for a side fraction f and band angle 45 degrees minus delta an exact dynamic programme over the columns maximises the number of squares; the best design is quenched once with Evan Daniel's ALM+SLP code from evand/square-packing search/packer at bb4cc78e, MIT, then random kicks of the coordinates and a further quench follow. This packing came from the design f = 0.913469, band angle 42.8 degrees (delta 2.2), tolerance 0, 45 tilted squares, column offset 0.96875, diagonal variant 14, quenched once to 16.890507465412 (11 s into a local run of the cloud job b2h269's command line), then kicked (sigma 0.0222) and quenched to 16.889734433328, then kicked again (sigma 0.001007) and quenched to the filed side 5 s into the kick run; the cloud job itself reached 16.88973007359575, but its pack file was lost, and the filed packing is the local re-find, 9e-14 higher. The filed packing has 45 tilted squares against the record's 100: one band at about 42.1 degrees and a small cluster at about -44.9 degrees at the upper-right end. They report, against the registry packing matched by assignment up to the square's symmetries: 261 of 269 centres move by more than 1e-3, 137 by more than 0.05 (largest 1.879); 121 squares re-tilted by more than 1 degree (largest 44.4); 45 squares tilted by more than 0.5 degree against the record's 100. The issue names the record T-290, its own #947, at side 16.9009945799513249, describing it in the claim paragraph as built from Nate Chaoweeraprasit's packing improved by Evan Daniel and PingYou Ltd and in the lineage paragraph as found by transplanting Evan Daniel's n = 304 packing, and names #962 (16.8994690758550465, adopted by PR #966 as T-296) as superseded with it. It states a side-only Kaggle leaderboard entry at 269, 16.889730079125 (team elegans, 5 November, cache of 9 November), 5.53e-9 above this side, unpublished. They ask that the improvement be credited to Doğa Özden, the band's source packing (n = 207 of the registry, n = 70 of Ryan Xu, improved by Evan Daniel and PingYou Ltd, and the lab's own n = 179 of #954) and the current record to their holders as the registry lists them, and the local optimizer to Evan Daniel. The issue says the search and its code were written and run by AI agents and that the checks were run by code that did not produce the packing; the issue and repository were prepared and posted by Özden's AI agent, which uses the account kenaznia-doga; Özden directed the work.
